title: Microsoft will raise cloud prices in India by nearly 16% and cut them in China from January

 Microsoft will raise cloud prices in India by nearly 16% and cut them in China from January
 Nov 16, 2026 
 · 
 2:55 AM 
 · 
 By MLQ.ai Newsroom · Edited by Peter Foy 
 · 
 2 min read 
 Key points 
 From Jan. 1, 2027, Microsoft's commercial cloud prices in Indian rupees rise 15.7% and on-premises prices rise by up to 20% [1] .
 Cloud prices in Chinese yuan fall by up to 8.5%, excluding Azure operated by 21Vianet; Australia falls 4%, Norway 5.9%, and New Zealand rises 10% [1] .
 It is the first round of Microsoft's annual currency review, announced in July, which replaces more frequent adjustments with one reset each January [1] [3] .
 Microsoft will raise commercial cloud prices billed in Indian rupees by 15.7% from Jan. 1, 2027, and on-premises software prices in rupees by up to 20%, according to a notice it posted to partners on Nov. 11 [1] . Cloud prices in Chinese yuan will fall by up to 8.5% [1] . The Register first reported the changes in its Asia roundup on Sunday [2] .
 Microsoft sells cloud services in local currencies at prices pegged to its US dollar list, and adjusts them as exchange rates move. The company said the changes "more closely align local currency pricing with global levels" [1] . Individual SKUs may differ slightly because of rounding, and the notice does not list new prices for specific products [1] .
 Five currencies change
 Currency Cloud change On-prem change 
 Indian rupee +15.7% Up to +20% 
 NZ dollar +10% +10% 
 Australian dollar -4% None 
 Norwegian krone -5.9% None 
 Chinese yuan Up to -8.5% None 
 Source: Microsoft Partner Center notice, Nov. 11, 2026; effective Jan. 1, 2027 [1] .
 The yuan cut covers Microsoft's global cloud services and Microsoft Cloud operated by 21Vianet, Microsoft's local partner in China, but excludes Microsoft Azure operated by 21Vianet [1] . The Register put the Australian cut at 4.5%; Microsoft's table says 4% [1] [2] .
 This is the first reset under the schedule Microsoft announced in July, when it said local currency prices for commercial cloud would be updated once a year, every Jan. 1, except in limited exceptional circumstances [3] . A rate set in January will therefore hold for the year even if a currency moves sharply. Microsoft said Brazilian real pricing will be reviewed after Brazil's tax reform takes effect, and Japanese yen pricing stays on an April cycle, with details for April 2027 due in February [1] .
